summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — ADSK +8%, NOW +7%, EXPE +7%, PLTR +7%, CHTR +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (SNDK -10%, CHRW -6%, UPS -6%, TXT -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (-9.96%) — Multi-day NAND/semiconductor rout plus WallStreetBets-fueled meme volatility; stock down ~31% since Thursday amid weak flash-memory pricing outlook ahead of Aug 5 earnings, no single company-specific news today. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded as an extreme-price/low-float, meme-volatility memory-chip name (~$1,293/share, 38x earnings) that doesn't fit standard large-cap tech or semiconductor universe screens.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-day analyst-driven rally: Guggenheim initiated ADSK at Buy w/ $245 PT (7/23) citing FY27 revenue upside; MaintainX acquisition and insider/institutional buying added momentum into 7/28.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ADSK is a large-cap design/engineering software name, a sector likely uncovered by the bot's current universes. Also the move built gradually over several sessions from sell-side coverage, not a single overnight gap a news-reactive gate would trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add design/engineering software (ADSK, PTC, ANSS) to the relevant sector universe, and add a rolling 5-day cumulative-return + analyst-initiation-count trigger to catch grind-up momentum that lacks a single-day gap.

top_movers.catalyst: 3rd/4th straight up day after Q2 beat (7/23): EPS $0.90 vs $0.86 est, raised FY26 guide, 50% of new biz now non-seat-based (eases AI-seat-erosion fear); broader SaaS 'AI rotation' rally lifted CRM/WDAY too.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — mega-cap enterprise SaaS name likely excluded by sector/category filters, and even if covered, a post-earnings-print cooldown window would have blocked entry on the initial gap day.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-drift override: names with 3+ consecutive up days ≥5% following an earnings beat get released into universe eligibility instead of being permanently excluded by sector/cap filters.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide travel rally as Strait of Hormuz reopening cut oil prices, plus a disclosed stake increase by Corient Private Wealth and lingering Q1 beat momentum.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EXPE likely falls in a large-cap consumer-discretionary/travel bucket not covered by the bot's tradable list, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap travel/OTA names (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB) to the universe with a sector-momentum tag so macro-driven sector rallies (e.g., oil-supply unwinds) can be captured going forward.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued rally into Aug 3 earnings — DIA withdrew its contested ASTRA solicitation after Palantir's protest, plus Oppenheimer reiterated a $200 target citing upside to 79% guided growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — PLTR is a mega-cap (~130x fwd earnings) AI/govt-software name that likely sits outside the sector/valuation buckets covered by the bot's static, periodically-refreshed universe lists.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a monthly universe-refresh screen (ADV > $500M, 3-month return > 30%) to surface high-momentum large caps like PLTR for inclusion review instead of relying solely on the fixed sector list.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued rebound after Q2 EPS beat ($10.66 vs $10.37 est, reported Jul 24) plus market pricing in nearing close of the $34.5B Charter-Cox merger (FCC-approved, targeted for August 2026).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a large-cap ($18-20B) legacy cable/telecom name whose price action is now dominated by a pending mega-merger (deal-completion/regulatory event risk), a profile most momentum/mean-reversion universes explicitly exclude via sector or M&A-overhang filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a merger-arb override that re-admits acquirer/target names to the universe once major deal contingencies clear (e.g., post-FCC approval), gated on realized volatility rather than a blanket telecom/M&A-pending exclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: No single dated news event found; DASH is up ahead of Aug 5 earnings amid a broad-market rotation out of sold-off chip/AI-infra names (Micron, AMD, Intel down 8-17%) into consumer-internet growth names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DASH sits in the consumer-discretionary/gig-economy internet-services bucket, not the tech-hardware/index-constituent universes the bot's momentum and mean-reversion strategies currently scan.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a consumer-internet/gig-economy sector bucket (DASH, UBER, ABNB) to the momentum universe with a sector-rotation trigger: flag names up >5% same-day a correlated basket (semis) sells off >5%.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-day NAND/semiconductor rout plus WallStreetBets-fueled meme volatility; stock down ~31% since Thursday amid weak flash-memory pricing outlook ahead of Aug 5 earnings, no single company-specific news today.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded as an extreme-price/low-float, meme-volatility memory-chip name (~$1,293/share, 38x earnings) that doesn't fit standard large-cap tech or semiconductor universe screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a semiconductor/memory-sector watchlist tier that admits high-priced, high-volatility names ahead of scheduled earnings (SNDK reports Aug 5) rather than filtering purely on market-cap/price-level bands.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued fallout from $604M Dallas jury verdict (CHRW 23% liable, post-Montgomery broker-liability precedent); Baird cut PT $230→$200 ahead of Q2 earnings due tomorrow.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap logistics broker). Even if covered, this is a litigation/legal-verdict driven move continuing from a Friday ruling, not a technical or earnings signal a momentum/news bot screens for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a litigation-headline gate flagging tickers tied to >$100M jury verdicts or precedent-setting liability rulings (e.g. 'Montgomery') for manual review, since verdict-driven selloffs often trend for multiple sessions.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS $1.76 beat $1.66 est. and FY guide raised, but stock fell on Q3 guidance: mid-single-digit domestic volume decline, Amazon volume glide-down, $891M transformation charges.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — UPS is a large-cap industrials/transport logistics name, a sector this bot's momentum/mean-reversion universes likely don't cover; also a scheduled-earnings gap-down, which favors pre-market positioning over post-close signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-calendar overlay that flags known large-cap reporters (transports/industrials) for a temporary universe inclusion around their print, gated on pre-market gap ≥5% at open.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS beat ($1.42 vs $1.33 est, rev $3.83B) but unchanged FY guidance, weak Aviation margins/cash flow, and MV-75 Cheyenne funding risk overshadowed the beat.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap industrials/aerospace conglomerate, not in tracked sector lists); also a same-day post-earnings gap-down where pre-market EPS-vs-margin nuance beats any post-open technical signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-day EPS-beat/guidance-miss scanner covering industrials/aerospace names outside current sector universes, gating entry on post-results gap ≤-5% within 30min of open.
